output.methodChoice: Evidence-ledger provenance check on the rollout comparison, then competing-hypotheses comparison against the long-range baseline (X6) and rollout history (X9).
output.brief: Last week's 5xx rate (0.41%) is within the service's normal range. Over the preceding 26 weeks the mean was 0.354% and the upper band edge 0.482%. Three earlier weeks were higher, and each was investigated with no fault found. The burn-rate page did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold), so the policy treats the week as normal. The dashboard count matches a raw-log recount, so this is not a counting artefact. The rollout comparison that points at v4.18 is misleading. Every recent rollout, including a config-only redeploy of an unchanged image, shows new pods erroring more than old ones. Cause: new pods start with a cold cache and time out against the replica. That adds only 10–20 errors per rollout, far less than the roughly 2,300 extra errors in the week. Bookings and complaints show no customer impact. Recommendation: don't roll back, and don't mute alerting. Muting would disable a protective control for no reason. Record the week as normal and run the standard check on the following week. If next week's rate goes above the band, investigate the replica move and partner-sync's month-end run. I can't rule those out, but there's no sign the rise needs action. Confidence is moderate to high.
